name: Respond.io
tagline: The Malaysia-based omnichannel messaging platform that pivoted from a chatbot startup into a 12-channel AI conversation hub, backed by $62.5M and genuine RAG-based hallucination controls.
tldr: Respond.io started in 2017 as Rocketbots, a Hong Kong chatbot-automation startup, relocated to Kuala Lumpur and rebranded in 2019 to focus on omnichannel customer conversations, and now serves 10,000+ businesses across 180 countries with $35M ARR and 169% year-on-year growth.

Pricing is per-workspace-plus-users: Starter $79/mo (5 users, 5,000 AI credits), Growth $159/mo (10 users, 10,000 AI credits, adds AI agents and workflow automation), Advanced $279/mo (20,000 AI credits, custom channels, SSO), and custom Enterprise — all with a 20% annual discount and AI included in every tier's credit allowance.

The channel list is genuinely exceptional: 12+ native channels including WhatsApp (with official Business Calling API support), Instagram, Facebook Messenger, Telegram, Viber, WeChat, LINE, SMS, TikTok, email, web chat, and VoIP calls unified in one inbox.

The AI Agent is built on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), grounding replies in approved knowledge sources with an explicit, user-controlled toggle for whether it can fall back to general knowledge when nothing relevant is found — a genuinely more transparent hallucination-control design than most competitors document.

Independent reviews are strongly positive (4.6/5 on Capterra) with structure and scale specifically praised, but a real, recurring complaint is that pricing is steep for small businesses, and at least one reviewer reports a denied refund request over downtime.

Best for mid-market to enterprise B2C teams running high-volume conversations across many messaging channels, especially WhatsApp — not for small teams on a tight budget, or anyone needing deep native ecommerce or website-builder integrations.
keyFeatures: An AI Agent that understands intent, learns from company knowledge sources, qualifies leads, updates CRM lifecycle stages, triggers workflows, and routes conversations by intent
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounding, with a user-toggleable setting controlling whether the AI can answer from general knowledge when nothing relevant exists in uploaded sources
Official WhatsApp Business Calling API support, including in-call transfers between agents without dropping the connection or losing context
Workflow automation (Growth tier and up) for routing, lifecycle updates, and multi-step conversation logic
Internal comments visible only to team members, attachable with supporting files, plus automatic AI-generated conversation summaries and closing notes on handoff
Snippets — reusable knowledge content (PDFs, URLs, text) that both AI Agents and human-facing AI Assist draw on for context-aware responses
Analytics covering resolution rates, response times, team performance, and conversion events synced via Meta's Conversions API for ad-attribution reporting
Zapier and Make integrations connecting to HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, and other CRMs, plus a developer API and webhooks on the Advanced tier

faq.question: How many channels does Respond.io actually support?
faq.answer: 12 or more, natively: WhatsApp (including official Business Calling API voice support), Instagram, Facebook Messenger, Telegram, Viber, WeChat, LINE, SMS, TikTok, email, a web chat widget, and VoIP calling, all unified in one inbox — one of the broadest native channel lists in this category.

faq.question: How does Respond.io prevent its AI Agent from hallucinating?
faq.answer: It uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground replies in approved knowledge sources before answering, and — distinctively — gives you an explicit toggle to control whether the AI can fall back to general knowledge when it can't find an answer in your uploaded content, or must stay strictly within your sources. That's a more transparent, user-controllable approach to the hallucination tradeoff than most competitors document.

faq.question: Can multiple languages work at once in Respond.io?
faq.answer: With real limitations. Each customer service agent can set a preferred language that incoming messages translate to, and Respond AI can translate incoming customer messages — but the platform is documented as supporting only one conversation language per agent, and a multilingual chatbot cannot handle several languages simultaneously. If your support volume genuinely spans many languages in parallel, test this limitation directly before committing.

faq.question: Does Respond.io integrate with Shopify or a CRM?
faq.answer: Shopify connects only through Zapier, with no dedicated native app found. CRM connectivity is broader — HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, and Pipedrive are all mentioned as connectable, though largely through Zapier/Make automation templates rather than confirmed deep native bidirectional sync for each one. Confirm the specific depth you need directly rather than assuming full native parity across every listed CRM.

faq.question: Is Respond.io affordable for a small business?
faq.answer: Not especially — this is a real, recurring theme in independent reviews. Starter is $79/month for 5 users, and pricing scales up through $159 and $279/month tiers before Enterprise, positioning this as a mid-market-to-enterprise tool. At least one reviewer specifically describes it as 'priced for larger organisations, not small businesses.'

faq.question: What is the most serious complaint on record about Respond.io?
faq.answer: Beyond general pricing concerns, one specific, documented complaint describes a customer requesting a full refund after the product was unusable during a downtime incident, which the company reportedly rejected. That's a concrete data point worth weighing alongside the otherwise strongly positive review base, particularly for any team considering an annual commitment.

pricingBreakdown: Respond.io's pricing reflects its mid-market-to-enterprise positioning clearly: $79/month for Starter is already above several competitors' entry points, and the jump to Growth ($159/mo) — where workflow automation and AI agents actually unlock — pushes real cost higher fast, especially once you factor in per-user overage fees ($12-24/month per additional seat depending on tier). The AI-credit model is worth understanding precisely: 5,000 credits included on Starter scaling to 40,000+ on Enterprise, which is a genuinely different metering unit than the flat per-resolution fees ($0.75-$1.00) common elsewhere in this category — model your expected AI usage against credits, not conversations, before comparing costs directly to a per-resolution competitor. Independent reviewers specifically flag this pricing level as a barrier for small businesses and freelancers, which tracks with the product's genuine strength: this is built for teams running real conversation volume across many channels, not a single-agent side project.

capabilities.note: This is Respond.io's clearest strength: 12+ native channels including a genuinely differentiated one — official WhatsApp Business Calling API support with in-call agent transfers — unified in a single inbox. Few competitors in this category match this breadth, particularly on the voice-over-WhatsApp capability.

Genuinely more sophisticated than most competitors' documented approach: RAG-based grounding in your own knowledge sources, combined with an explicit, user-controlled toggle for whether the AI can fall back to general knowledge or must stay strictly within your uploaded content. That transparency about the accuracy-versus-coverage tradeoff is a real differentiator, even though there's no independently audited resolution rate to pair with it.

Beyond standard resolution and response-time metrics, syncing conversion events via Meta's Conversions API is a distinctive, genuinely useful capability for any team running WhatsApp or Messenger ad campaigns and wanting to tie ad spend to actual conversation outcomes.

A real gap worth being direct about: Shopify connects only through Zapier with no dedicated native app, and there's no WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, or Webflow integration at all. If deep ecommerce order-data access or website-builder integration matters to your use case, this isn't where Respond.io is strong.

Structurally built for teams with real conversation volume and budget — Starter at $79/month with per-user overages puts this meaningfully above several competitors' entry pricing, and independent reviewers consistently describe it as steep for smaller organizations.

verdict: Respond.io's evolution from a 2017 Hong Kong chatbot startup into a $35M-ARR omnichannel messaging platform tracks the market it's built for: real, high-volume B2C conversation management across more channels than almost any competitor in this category, including a genuinely distinctive official WhatsApp Business Calling API implementation with in-call agent transfers. The AI Agent backs up that ambition with real sophistication — it qualifies leads, updates CRM lifecycle stages, and routes by intent, grounded in a RAG-based knowledge system with an unusually transparent, user-controlled toggle for the general-knowledge-fallback tradeoff most competitors don't let you configure explicitly. Where I'd push back is cost: this is priced for the mid-market-to-enterprise teams it's clearly built for, and independent reviewers are specific and consistent that it's steep for a small business or freelancer, with real per-user overage costs stacking on top of an already-elevated base tier. There's also a genuine, documented limitation worth knowing before you commit: the platform supports only one conversation language per agent, and a multilingual chatbot can't handle several languages at once — worth testing directly if your support volume genuinely spans many languages in parallel. And while there's no independently audited AI resolution rate, at least one reviewer's account of a denied refund during a downtime incident is a concrete data point worth weighing alongside the otherwise strong 4.6/5 review base. My honest read: if your team runs real conversation volume across many channels — especially WhatsApp, including voice — and has the budget this tier of tool assumes, Respond.io's channel breadth and AI sophistication are genuinely hard to match. If you're a small team or need deep ecommerce/website-builder integration, this isn't built for you specifically.
